cards.text: It's the Feast of Tabernacles in Jerusalem, and Jesus has been teaching in the temple courts (John 7:2, 14). The chief priests and Pharisees have already sent officers to arrest Him (John 7:32). Now it's the last and greatest day of the feast, and friend, the air is TENSE.
Jesus stands up and calls out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.” A LOUD voice, friend, the kind Mags would be proud of.

cards.question: Jesus says streams of living water will flow from within someone. Who?
John explains it for us. When Jesus talks about living water, He's speaking about the ___.
John says those who believed in Jesus were later to receive the Spirit, but the Spirit had not yet been given. Why not?

answers.text: Jesus had not yet been glorified
The feast had not ended yet
The crowd had not repented yet

cards.text: Some people hear those words and say, “This is truly the Prophet.” Friend, ONE loud invitation and folks are already handing out titles.

cards.question: Some in the crowd call Jesus the Prophet. Others give a different answer. Who do they say He is?

cards.text: But still others push back, and their problem is where Jesus is from. That's like turning down the best cookie in the box because you don't like the bakery on the label.

cards.question: The doubters in the crowd ask how the Christ could come from one place. Which place?
The doubters point to Scripture. They say the Christ will come from the line of ___ and from the village of ___.
Jesus' words leave the crowd divided because of Him.
Some in the crowd want to seize Jesus, and someone finally lays a hand on Him.

cards.text: Now the officers head back to the chief priests and Pharisees with nothing in their hands, like showing up to the meeting without the ONE thing you were sent to get. The bosses ask, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”

cards.question: The chief priests and Pharisees want to know why the officers didn't bring Jesus in. What do the officers say?

answers.text: Never has anyone spoken like this man
Never has anyone drawn a crowd like this
Never has anyone stood up to us like this

cards.question: When the officers say no one has ever spoken like Jesus, the Pharisees agree and decide to go hear Him for themselves.
The Pharisees ask the officers if they've been deceived too, and whether any rulers or Pharisees have believed in Jesus. Then they say the crowd that doesn't know the law is under a ___.

cards.text: Then Nicodemus speaks up, a man who had gone to Jesus earlier (John 3:1-2) and who is one of them. Friend, I bet every head at that table just turned.

cards.question: Nicodemus asks the group a question about their own law. What does he ask?

answers.text: Whether it convicts a man before hearing him
Whether it lets officers arrest at a feast
Whether it allows healing on the Sabbath

cards.question: Nicodemus asks whether their law convicts a man without hearing him first. How do the others answer him?

answers.text: They ask if he is from Galilee too
They agree to give Jesus a hearing
They send Nicodemus to question Jesus

cards.text: Then they tell him, “Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.” Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story's still got another batch in the oven.

findings.problem: The joke says the doubters turn Jesus down because they 'don't like the bakery on the label.' That gives them a reason the text doesn't give. The text says their objection comes from Scripture: the Christ is to come from David's line and from Bethlehem (John 7:42). Treating a Scripture-based objection as label snobbery makes fun of them instead of looking at their situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The comparison adds a motive (dislike of where Jesus is from) that the text doesn't state. In John 7:41-42, the doubters say only that Scripture places the Christ in David's line and in Bethlehem.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The choice card packs three moments into its question: the Pharisees asking if the officers have been deceived (v47), asking whether any rulers or Pharisees have believed (v48), and the curse line (v49). No story card tells verses 47-48. They are squeezed into the question as setup, so this one card carries several beats instead of one question.

rule.text: One beat per card. A story card carries one moment of the passage. A choice card is one question and its answers.
